text: Why can't the government just print a million dollars for every person, and make everyone rich?
America has about three hundred forty-two million people.
A million dollars each? That's three hundred forty-two trillion dollars.
Now, all the money in America right now? About twenty-three trillion.
So we'd be making almost fifteen times more money than exists.
But here's the problem. The stuff doesn't multiply.
Same houses. Same burgers. Same gallons of gas.
Now everyone walks in with a million, and every seller knows it.
The burger guy raises his price. Then the landlord. Then the gas station.
Prices keep climbing, and your million buys way less than you thought.
This isn't just theory. Zimbabwe printed so much money, it issued a one hundred trillion dollar note.
So what does America actually print?
The Federal Reserve orders about four to five billion new bills a year, to replace worn-out cash and meet demand.
That's roughly a hundred and nine to a hundred and forty billion dollars. Not three hundred forty-two trillion.
Money only works because there's less of it than the things you can buy.
So if everyone gets a million, nobody actually gets richer.
Would you still take the million? Tell me in the comments.
